text:
maria-devex: FYI running into a weird behavior when swapping service account contexts in our Node streaming client. open to quick ideas — I set up OIDC JWTs per-project but streams sometimes get a 401 mid-stream and don't auto-reauth.

kevin-sdk: can you paste the refresh flow? are you using a token provider that renews before expiry or only on 401?

maria-devex: using a simple provider that does on-demand exchange:
```js
async function getIdToken(saKey, aud) {
  const jwt = signJwt(saKey, {aud, exp: Math.floor(Date.now()/1000)+3600});
  const resp = await fetch('https://oauth.example/token', {method:'POST', body: jwt});
  return resp.id_token;
}
```
We call this when we detect a different project scope. works for requests but streaming connection sometimes hangs and then receives 401.

kevin-sdk: ah — two things: 1) streaming sockets need preemptive rotation, not only on 401 (the server will close mid-stream rather than accept a re-exchange). 2) Node http(s).Agent keepalive can hold onto old auth headers if you reuse the same agent + socket pool.

sam-backend: +1 on the keepalive. In Python we saw the same: reusing Requests Session kept auth in connection. Workaround was to create a fresh client/transport when changing SA scope.

lee-ml: also check the token's "sub"/"iss" claims. If you mint an id_token with the service account as subject but change project/audience, some routers reject it even if signed. We ended up normalizing audience to the platform client-id (single value) and enforcing project in a header/arg.

maria-devex: hmm — we were swapping audience per-project. Might try single audience + project header. Does the SDK have a pattern for rotation and reconnect?

kevin-sdk: yes — our Node SDK has a small helper:
```js
// pseudo
const client = new RedwoodStreamClient({tokenProvider});
client.on('auth_expiring', async () => {
  await client.rotateToken(await tokenProvider());
});
// if you change project: client = client.withScope(newScope) // returns new instance
```
If you can't create a new instance, call client.gracefulClose() then new client. That clears Agent pools.

maria-devex: any guidance on retry/backoff for the stream connect vs in-stream errors? we do exponential backoff but worried about token storms when many clients rotate simultaneously.

sam-backend: we debounce token refreshes at the infra layer — only one refresh per service-account per 30s. Also add jitter on reconnects.

lee-ml: for streaming that preserves a KV cache, you may want to use a resume token: the server can accept a resume_id + new auth to continue without full replay. check server supports it (our platform does behind a flag).

maria-devex: good to know. quick Q: is there a recommended expiry window to force preemptive rotation? we saw 1m left cause failures on flaky networks.

kevin-sdk: we schedule rotation at TTL * 0.8 or when remaining <= 90s, whichever is earlier. That helped.

ci-bot: Deployment check: new client branch with preemptive-rotation landed to canary (build 452): https://ci.internal/452 — please smoke test. :rocket:

maria-devex: thanks! I'll try: 1) switch to single audience + project header, 2) preemptive rotate at 0.8 TTL, 3) create new client instance when scope changes. Will report back. :thumbsup:

kevin-sdk: if you want a quick diff, ping me and I can open a small PR with the client-with-scope helper.

sam-backend: FYI for Python folks: the pattern is similar — recreate aiohttp.ClientSession or disable keepalive when you switch SA.

maria-devex: one more odd log snippet in case it's useful:
```
[stream] warn: AUTH_EXPIRED mid-stream - closing (status=401)
[stream] info: reconnect attempt=1 backoff=300ms
[stream] error: reconnect failed - token mismatch
```
kevin-sdk: "token mismatch" usually means the server saw token A then the client retried with token B on same socket. New socket = new TLS connection = clean.

maria-devex: got it. thanks all, will try the client instance approach and report.

lee-ml: ping if you need help validating claims or test tokens.

maria-devex: will do. closing loop after canary smoke.
